name: St Mark's Basilica
_about: ST MARK'S BASILICA, Venice (1063-94; the lead domes about 1230, the Gothic crown about 1400): the five domes on a Greek cross, each a crossing under a `drum-dome` on the onion section, lantern and cross; the west front of five deep portals, columns in two tiers and gold mosaic lunettes, the terrace and four horses, five arches under ogee gables with their leaves and statues, tabernacles between; the narthex; the Campanile, its Loggetta and the Piazza's paving. Generated by tools/archgen/st_marks.py -- edit the script for arithmetic changes. West is -z, north +x.

body._about: the church's outer walls on the cross and the narthex's rectangle, faced in marble, windows high in them; on the west the five doors

narthex back wall._about: the wall between the narthex and the nave, with the great door and two lesser

treasury wall._about: the walls between the west arm and, north, the narthex's arm, south, the Treasury and Baptistery

middle piers._about: each dome's four piers, rising over the roofs

middle arches._about: its four barrel arches, pier to pier, their backs in lead over the flat roofs

middle dome._about: the high outer dome the Venetians raised over the low brick one: lead on timber, gently bulging, on its ring of windows

middle lantern._about: the small bulbous lantern on each dome and the gold cross on it

west tympana._about: the lunettes closing a dome's outer arches over the roofs, three windows in each

roof 1._about: the flat lead roofs round the domes

nave columns._about: the marble columns that separate the arms from their aisles

apse._about: the main apse behind the high altar, its half dome roofed in lead

side apses._about: the two smaller apses beside it

portal orders._about: the front's outer arch, a portal's first order

portal recesses._about: the deep recess behind it, its second order: 2m through, the door and the lunette at its back

west lunette 1._about: the mosaic over each door, on the wall at the recess's back: the Last Judgment over the middle one, the bringing of St Mark's body from Alexandria over the four others

lower columns 1._about: two tiers of precious marble columns, brought from the East after 1204, on the piers and down the portals' sides: three stones, porphyry, verde antico, grey

column course._about: the course between the tiers, on each pier

arch rings._about: the carved band round each portal's arch

terrace._about: the terrace over the lower register, where the horses stand

terrace balusters._about: the marble balustrade along the terrace

horses._about: the four gilded horses of the Hippodrome, four abreast over the middle door, drawn in bars at their real 2.3m (one part: bars touch only as one piece)

south upper wall._about: the upper wall either side of the middle window, its top the ogee gables of two bays

north upper wall._about: the upper wall either side of the middle window, its top the ogee gables of two bays

middle window wall._about: the great window over the horses: blind until the fire of 1419

middle gable._about: the great ogee over it, St Mark and the angels on its point

upper lunette 1._about: the four upper mosaics: the Descent from the Cross, the Harrowing, the Resurrection, the Ascension

window panes._about: the great window's dark glass (a pane stood in for it: what's behind it is the west dome's piers)

upper rings._about: a carved marble band round each upper arch

gable leaves 1._about: the Gothic crown: carved leaves climbing every gable's edges, white and gold

gable statues._about: the four warrior saints on the side gables

st mark foot._about: St Mark on the great gable

tabernacles._about: the six tabernacles on the piers between the gables, their spires' figures for the Evangelists, the Virgin and Gabriel

north flank gables._about: the Gothic crown continued along the flanks

campanile shaft._about: the Campanile's shaft, 12m square and 50m of brick, rebuilt 1902-12 as it was

campanile strips._about: the brick pilaster strips, five to a face

campanile belfry._about: the belfry: four arches to a side, in white Istrian stone, the five bells within

campanile attic._about: the attic over the belfry, its reliefs of Venice as Justice and the Lion of St Mark

loggetta._about: Sansovino's Loggetta against the east face, three arches of red Verona and white marble

piazza._about: the paving of the Piazza and the Piazzetta: pale Istrian bands on grey trachyte, in tiles so no one triangle of it is vast
